transcript: Last night I was at the first preview of Purlie Victorious, starring Leslie Odom Jr. In the titular role. The premise is that Purlie is a preacher trying to take back his community’s church in his Georgia hometown with the help of Lutiebelle Gussie Jenkins, a woman posing as Purlie’s cousin so they can collect an inheritance from a local plantation owner. This comedy by Ossie Davis originally premiered in 1961, but so much of the text is richly poetic and still abundantly relevant today. This production is simple, and it lets the text breathe and the actors breathe life into it. I thought the acting from everyone was really great. Leslie Odom Jr. Certainly does not disappoint in this play, but to me, the real standout in this production is Kara Young as Lutiebelle. Her performance is so captivating and layered, and she hilariously steals multiple scenes As she gears up to impersonate a woman she never met and has little in common with. Overall, I think this play was really worth reviving, and I would definitely recommend going. It's funny, it's well paced, it's well acted, and it's under two hours with no intermission, which I love. It's running basically through the end of 2023, so put it on your radar for this fall with that another playbill for my collection.
